sources.title: Reading room discovery notes
sources.content:
# Reading room discovery notes

14 July 2027 — Bracken Civic Library, ReadingLight pilot

ReadingLight will help visitors find space in the library's two reading rooms. Researcher Mira Fen recorded six visitor interviews and two afternoon observations at this branch. Four interviewees said they had abandoned a room after finding no seat; observers counted nine unnecessary room entries. These are local observations, not evidence about all library users. Librarian Oren Vale suspects that a live seat map would reduce interruptions across other branches; nobody has tested that market hypothesis. Weekend and screen-reader users have not yet been interviewed. That gap limits demand claims but does not prevent a staff-only prototype.

Product steward Sela Rowan accepted decision D-041 today: prototype individual free/occupied seat dots, without visitor names, in these two rooms. This authorizes prototype design only. Any visitor-facing deployment requires a separate written release approval from release chair Ivo Reed.

sources.title: Prototype review and design correspondence
sources.content:
# Prototype review and design correspondence

19 July 2027 — ReadingLight review, signed by product steward Sela Rowan

I approve decision D-052, replacing D-041 for both pilot rooms. Staff will choose one availability band: “none,” “a few,” or “several.” Availability detail in every display, stored record, and analytics event is limited to the band and room identifier; individual seat identifiers and exact seat counts are prohibited. Visitors could otherwise infer where a person is sitting in our small rooms. Show an update time and mark information stale after ten minutes. This is the accepted prototype design; it does not authorize visitor deployment. The research coverage gap remains open and does not block this design work.

21 July 2027 — Designer Nessa Clay's circulated concept

My revised concept offers a much clearer per-seat map, exact vacancy count, and automatic seat-level history. It could improve confidence and produce a stronger demo. Sela has not reviewed or approved it. Please treat this as a discussion draft for next week's workshop.
